Okay, so here's what happened with the outage last night. At around 9:15, the API gateway started returning 500 errors for about 10% of requests, and the on-call engineer got paged. She looked at the dashboards and saw that the connection pool to the primary database was maxed out, so the first thing she did was restart the gateway pods, which made it a little better but not really. Then we noticed that a deploy had gone out at 9:05, that changed the default query timeout from 5 seconds to 30 seconds, and that meant slow queries were holding connections open six times longer than before, which is why the pool filled up. We rolled back the deploy at 9:40 and the errors went away within a couple of minutes.

So the root cause is basically that change plus the fact that we have no alert on pool saturation. The follow-ups are to:
- Add that alert.
- Put the timeout behind a feature flag.
- Add a load test to the release checklist that would have caught this.

I also think we should review how config changes get approved, because this one went through with only a single reviewer and it looked harmless in the diff. And I'll write all of this up properly tomorrow and share it with the team.

The fast model comes back in under 100 milliseconds for short takes and a few hundred for long ones, and the thorough model is about 7 times slower but it fixes more of the awkward phrasing.

The problem is the deadline. When a take is long, the thorough model runs out of time and we throw away its answer, so the user gets the raw text instead, and that happens more than it should.

There are two things I want to try:

2. Make sure the model is warm before the first take so we don't pay for loading on top of the generation.

I also want to look at why the guard rejects some outputs, because a few of those look fine to me when I read them side by side. We should be careful there, though. The guard exists so we never lose a sentence or change what someone meant, so anything we loosen needs a test.

records.delivered: Okay, so here's what happened with the outage last night. At around 9:15, the API gateway started returning 500 errors for about 10% of requests, and the on-call engineer got paged. She looked at the dashboards and saw that the connection pool to the primary database was maxed out. So, the first thing she did was restart the gateway pods, which made it a little better, but not really. Then we noticed that a deploy had gone out at 9:05 that changed the default query timeout from 5 seconds to 30 seconds, and that meant slow queries were holding connections open six times longer than before, which is why the pool filled up. We rolled back the deploy at 9:40, and the errors went away within a couple of minutes. So, the root cause is basically that change plus the fact that we have no alert on pool saturation. The follow-ups are to add that alert, to put the timeout behind a feature flag, and to add a load test to the release checklist that would have caught this. I also think we should review how config changes get approved because this one went through with only a single reviewer, and it looked harmless in the diff. I'll write all of this up properly tomorrow and share it with the team.

Okay, this is a longer note for the team about the benchmark results. We ran the cleanup models one at a time on the same machine, and the numbers are mostly what we expected. The fast model comes back in under 100 milliseconds for short takes and a few hundred for long ones, and the thorough model is about seven times slower, but it fixes more of the awkward phrasing. The problem is the deadline. When a take is long, the thorough model runs out of time, and we throw away its answer, so the user gets the raw text instead, and that happens more than it should.

There are two things I want to try:
1. Give long takes a bigger budget that scales with the number of words.
2. Make sure the model is warm before the first take so we don't pay for loading on top of the generation.

I also want to look at why the guard rejects some outputs, because a few of those look fine to me when I read them side by side. We should be careful there, though; the guard exists so we never lose a sentence or change what someone meant, so anything we loosen needs a test.

She looked at the dashboards and saw that the connection pool to the primary database was maxed out, so the first thing she did was restart the gateway pods, which made it a little better but not really. Then we noticed that a deploy had gone out at 9:05, that changed the default query timeout from 5 seconds to 30 seconds, and that meant slow queries were holding connections open six times longer than before, which is why the pool filled up. We rolled back the deploy at 9:40 and the errors went away within a couple of minutes.

So the root cause is basically that change plus the fact that we have no alert on pool saturation. The follow-ups are to:
- Add that alert.
- Put the timeout behind a feature flag.
- Add a load test to the release checklist that would have caught this.

I also think we should review how config changes get approved, because this one went through with only a single reviewer and it looked harmless in the diff. And I'll write all of this up properly tomorrow and share it with the team.

The fast model comes back in under 100 milliseconds for short takes and a few hundred for long ones, and the thorough model is about 7 times slower but it fixes more of the awkward phrasing.
